For wheat, I will use improved seed rather than traditional seed, because I want more stable yield and better use of fertilizer and irrigation. I will put in a moderate-to-strong fertilizer rate since my goal is dependable production, not low-input farming. I will irrigate wheat several times because in Hebei the wheat season often needs water support, especially for tillering, jointing, and grain filling. I will do rotary tillage because it is practical for my scale and easier to manage with limited household labor when some family members work off-farm. I will spray a limited number of times, only enough to protect yield.

For maize, I will also use the same 5.0 mu right after wheat harvest. I will choose hybrid maize because that is what I would rely on for stronger yield. I will keep fertilizer input a bit higher on nitrogen for maize than for wheat, since maize responds strongly to it, while keeping phosphorus and potassium at moderate levels. Because I have well irrigation, I will plan for a couple of irrigations if rainfall is not enough. I will keep rotary tillage here too, mainly for speed and simplicity between wheat harvest and maize planting. My whole plan is to stay with a familiar, yield-focused system that fits my farm size, my labor situation, and the irrigation access I already have.
